c

It is proposed to send a spacecraft to Jupiter. The spacecraft would be launched to a point Q far from Earth and would then be accelerated by the pressure of the Sun’s radiation on a sail attached to the spacecraft. The following data are available:

total mass of spacecraft = 1400 kg

sail area = 1600 m2

solar radiation intensity at Q = 420 W m−2

c.i Show that the acceleration of the spacecraft at Q due to solar radiation alone is about 3 × 10–6 m s–2. [2]

c.ii The distance between Q and Jupiter is 6.1 × 1011 m. Estimate the time, in years, it would take the spacecraft to reach Jupiter, assuming that the spacecraft moves with the acceleration in (i). [2]

c.iii State one reason why the acceleration of the spacecraft will not be constant. [1]

d

The spacecraft enters an elliptical orbit around Jupiter.



At the position shown, the spacecraft has its maximum orbital speed.

d.i Draw, on the diagram, a possible position of Jupiter. [1]

d.ii Explain your answer to (d)(i). [2]

e

The spacecraft changes its orbit into a circular orbit just above the surface of Jupiter, so that the orbit radius is essentially equal to the radius of Jupiter.

e.i Show that the orbital period, , of the spacecraft is given by , where is the density of Jupiter. [3]

e.ii The orbital period is 2.9 hours. Estimate the density of Jupiter. [2]
